title: Bram and the Inheritance
premise: Ulyana Eastwick, concierge of the Bramwell Grand, has spent two decades cataloguing the town's secrets in a private ledger — until a murdered stranger is found wearing clothes stolen from Ulyana's own closet, and a detective discovers the ledger. As suspicion falls on him and the trial date looms, Ulyana realizes the killer is someone who once worked at the hotel and learned his filing system from the inside: his estranged protégé, Dara Voss, who is framing him to bury her own role in a death twenty years ago that Ulyana helped cover up. In the end, Ulyana trades his silence about the old crime for evidence that convicts Dara, loses the hotel he called home, and finally learns that belonging bought with secrets was never belonging at all.
about_author: Mirabel Oyelaran spent eight years working night desks at grand hotels across three countries, collecting the small betrayals of guests and staff alike before turning them into fiction. She lives above a shuttered inn she refuses to explain.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet the Bramwell Grand through its concierge's ritual: keys, complaints, and the locked drawer where twenty years of secrets are filed A to Z. The emotional beat is quiet pride — Ulyana believes his vigilance protects everyone. It ends with police arriving at dawn: a body in the service stairwell, dressed in Ulyana's spare suit.

chapters.title: A Suit That Fits Too Well
chapters.summary: Detective Imre Kade's POV as she interviews Ulyana, who notices everything except how guilty he sounds. The victim is unidentified; the clothes are unmistakably Ulyana's. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen for the first time. Kade finds nothing incriminating yet, but leaves with the sense that Ulyana is performing innocence rather than possessing it.

chapters.title: Drawer F
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. He races home to move the ledger before a search warrant lands, but finds it disturbed — pages from Drawer F, the file on a 2005 death ruled accidental, are missing. Emotional beat: dread curdling into recognition. Whoever took them knows his system intimately. He suspects the hotel's former night manager, Dara Voss, who vanished fifteen years ago.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. She identifies the victim: a retired insurance investigator who had been asking quiet questions about the 2005 death. Kade begins to suspect Ulyana is not the killer but a target — or an accomplice. Emotional beat: reluctant respect between adversaries. She confronts Ulyana with the victim's last appointment book; his name is written inside the cover.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, flashing back to 2005: a young chambermaid died after a fall the hotel hushed up, and Ulyana filed the truth instead of reporting it. Emotional beat: shame surfacing after decades of order. He admits to himself that Dara saw everything back then — and taught her that information is currency. The chapter ends with a note slipped under his door: 'You still alphabetize.'

chapters.title: The Trial Date
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. The prosecutor, pressured by the hotel's owner, charges Ulyana to close the case fast; trial set in six weeks. Kade doubts the theory but follows procedure. Emotional beat: institutional pressure versus instinct. She notices the crime scene was staged with knowledge only a former employee would have — the camera blind spots, the stairwell timing — and quietly reopens the 2005 file.

chapters.title: Dara
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. He tracks Dara Voss to a neighboring town, where she works under another name. Their confrontation is the novel's midpoint: she confesses she killed the investigator, who had discovered she caused the 2005 death, and she framed Ulyana because he taught her that whoever holds the file holds the power. Emotional beat: grief and recognition — she is what he made. He flees without calling Kade.

chapters.title: Confessions Are Evidence
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. Ulyana finally comes to her, offering his confession about 2005 and Dara's name — knowing it may destroy him too. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal. Kade verifies enough to act but warns him that his admission could sink the case against Dara. They agree on a trap: bait Dara with the one page she never found, hidden in Drawer Z.

chapters.title: The Last Filing Error
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Kade POVs during the trap at the hotel. Dara comes for the page; Kade takes her alive, but Dara forces Ulyana to choose between saving Kade and destroying the ledger forever. Emotional beat: climax — power confronted with consequence. Ulyana burns the ledger to save Kade, surrendering his archive and his armor. Dara is arrested; the trial collapses into a plea.

chapters.title: Checkout
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue-like. He pleads to obstruction in the 2005 cover-up, serves community time, and leaves the Bramwell Grand for good — no longer its keeper of secrets. Kade visits; something like friendship, unfiled. Emotional beat: bittersweet release. Belonging, he understands now, cannot be catalogued or purchased; it has to be risked. He checks out of his own life and walks into the ordinary morning.
